findings.issue_text: P1: Denial cache is never invalidated when permissions change (service.go ~line 153, s.permDenialCache.Set) — users remain denied for up to shortCacheTTL after access is granted, because the denial entry short-circuits Check with Allowed: false before permCache is consulted

P1: Denial cache entry takes precedence over a fresh allow and over an updated permCache (service.go ~line 117) — the denial lookup runs before getCachedIdentityPermissions and only the allow path has outdated-cache fallback, making false denials sticky and uncorrectable by existing invalidation

P2: Denial cache key collides when Name/ParentFolder are empty (rbac/cache.go ~line 30, service.go ~line 117) — key concatenation without boundary separator means "dash1_"+"fold" equals "dash"+"_1fold", and empty-field keys can deny unrelated resource-less checks for the same user/action

P2: List swallows non-cache-miss errors from getCachedIdentityPermissions (service.go ~line 180) — any error is treated as cache miss and retried via getIdentityPermissions, masking transient identity-lookup errors and hiding root causes from logs/metrics

P3: In-process client silently loses its cache (rbac.go ~line 101) — ProvideAuthZClient switches newRBACClient's LocalCache (30s expiry) to NoopCache, so every check now pays full server-side processing

P3: permDenialCache.Set return error is ignored (service.go ~line 153) — the cache set error is discarded without logging, unlike surrounding code, so a persistently failing cache silently degrades with no observability
New permDenialCache is never included in permission-change invalidation hooks, so stale deny entries can bypass permission grants for up to shortCacheTTL (pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:~153)
userPermDenialCacheKey omits checkReq.IdentityType, causing user and service-account identities with the same UID to share denial cache entries (pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30-32)
Denial-cache lookup short-circuits before cached permissions, letting a cached deny override a fresh cached allow (service.go:116-137)
Cached-permissions fast path never populates the denial cache when allowed == false, making cache-fill order affect behavior (service.go:116-137)
getCachedIdentityPermissions returns cache.ErrNotFound for TypeRenderService, silently skipping the cache fast path; also, real errors silently fall through to the full DB path (service.go:~349)

Unbounded cache cardinality: permDenialCache keys include specific resource name and parent, so every denied check on a distinct resource creates a new per-user/action/resource cache entry, causing key-space and memory blowup

Denial cache is not invalidated on permission/role changes: after a user is granted access to a previously denied resource, the stale deny entry short-circuits Check and returns Allowed: false until TTL expiry

Errors from getCachedIdentityPermissions are silently swallowed in Check; real errors (GetUserIdentifiers failure, unsupported identity type) are discarded and redundant work is done before re-encountering them in getIdentityPermissions

Metric mislabeling on cache-hit-then-deny path: permissionCacheUsage 'false'/'true' is emitted after a store fetch even though the cache was used, distorting cache-usage metrics on the deny-via-cached-perms path
Denial cache is never invalidated on permission changes, causing stale deny results after access is granted; it must participate in the same invalidation flow as permCache
Denial cache key uses raw UserUID without distinguishing identity type, so anonymous checks (empty UserUID) collapse onto shared keys causing cross-identity denial sharing
Denial cache key fields joined with '_' without escaping can collide (e.g., name='a_b', parent='c' vs name='a', parent='b_c'), producing incorrect deny results

getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions no longer consult the cache after cache lookup moved to getCachedIdentityPermissions; other internal callers silently lose caching, changing the prior self-caching contract with no compile-time signal

Stale denial entries deny access even after a permission grant because the denial cache is checked first and uses a different cache key that is not refreshed by permission-cache invalidation, extending the stale-denial window

Cache-hit denial path defeats the purpose of the cache: when permCache is hit but denied, code falls through to a full DB fetch before populating the denial cache, so denials are uncached on first hit and add DB load
List treats non-NotFound errors from getCachedIdentityPermissions as cache misses, masking the root error, duplicating user-identifier lookups, and paying two failing DB paths on persistent failure
permDenialCache.Set error is silently ignored, so with a distributed cache backend the denial cache may silently never warm
Denial cache key concatenates userUID, action, name, and parent with unescaped '_' separators, allowing key collisions that can deny access to the wrong resource
In-process client switched to NoopCache so service-level caches are the only caching; code relying on client-level cache to absorb bursts now hits the store directly — verify this deliberate change

P1: permDenialCache in pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116-160 has no invalidation path when user permissions change, causing stale denials (potential access bug) after permission grants until shortCacheTTL expires

P1: Test at service_test.go:943-963 ('Fallback to the database on outdated cache') tests an ordinary cache miss, not the actual stale-denial scenario (denial cache entry for a resource that has since been granted), masking the missing invalidation coverage
P2: The cached-deny fallthrough path in Check (service.go:116-141) — cache hit with allowed=false falling through to a full getIdentityPermissions fetch before caching the denial — is untested

P2: New getCachedIdentityPermissions edge branches (TypeAnonymous, TypeRenderService, default error) in service.go:342-368 are untested; the default branch changes observable behavior since errors are silently swallowed in Check/List, causing a second doomed fetch
P3: New exported NoopCache in pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:238-251 has zero test coverage
P3: TestService_CacheList (service_test.go:1291-1324) covers only the cache-hit branch; the cache-miss List fallback path (cache.ErrNotFound → store consultation) is untested

Duplicated identity-type/cache-key resolution logic between getCachedIdentityPermissions and getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions risks divergence; extract a shared resolvePermissionCacheKey helper

Silent error swallowing in Check and List: errors from getCachedIdentityPermissions are indistinguishable from cache miss and silently fall through to DB path with no logging; distinguish cache.ErrNotFound from real errors and log/track unexpected ones

Double identifier/DB lookup on cache miss in Check: getCachedIdentityPermissions resolves GetUserIdentifiers before discovering perm cache is empty, then fallback getIdentityPermissions resolves identifiers again

NoopCache defined locally in pkg/services/authz/rbac.go instead of being contributed to the cache package/authzlib; NewClient's caller-supplied cache API forces a noop stub, and the caching asymmetry between in-process and remote clients is implicit with no comment

Cache orchestration concerns inlined into Check handler while List uses a different, inconsistent caching pattern (no denial cache); caching policy should live in the permission-resolution layer, not each handler

permissionCacheUsage metric semantics become confusing/misleading after refactor: 'false' no longer uniformly means served-from-store, increments occur at a different layer, and label pairs mean different things per branch, changing dashboard/alert meaning without version bump

Deleted test coverage for cache-hit behavior in getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions: removed 'should return permissions from cache if available' case leaves internal cache-read behavior untested, especially anonymous permission caching which has no equivalent new test

P1: Denial cache is never invalidated and overrides fresh allow decisions — cached denial wins even when permission cache says allow, and with no invalidation path permission grants are blocked for up to shortCacheTTL; denial key also lacks permission-version so stale-permission denials can poison granted permissions (pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:117,153)

P2: Denial cache key collision via unescaped _/: delimiters — userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates action, name, parent with _ and no escaping, so distinct tuples collide and a denial for one resource silently denies another (pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30-32)

P2: Denial cached for checks with empty Name blankets all unnamed checks — a transiently incomplete permission fetch can poison cache for all subsequent unnamed user/action/folder checks until TTL expiry (pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:117,153)

P3: Denial-cache hit path skips identity re-validation — denial keyed on raw checkReq.UserUID is returned before GetUserIdentifiers resolution, so UID reuse after user deletion inherits the old denial (pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:117-121)

P3: Coverage silently removed for the old cache-hit path — the test asserting getUserPermissions returns cached permissions was deleted without an equivalent assertion that the singleflight path still consults permCache (pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:342-349)

goldens.comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.
The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Denial cache is never invalidated when permissions change (service.go ~line 153, s.permDenialCache.Set) — users remain denied for up to shortCacheTTL after access is granted, because the denial entry short-circuits Check with Allowed: false before permCache is consulted

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, a denial cache entry (`permDenialCache`) is consulted first and immediately returns `Allowed: false` if present, before any permission cache or DB lookup ("explicit cache deny entry" path). The code only ever adds entries (`s.permDenialCache.Set(...)` when `!allowed`) and never deletes/invalidates them on subsequent allowed results or permission changes. This means a previously denied `(namespace,user,action,name,parentFolder)` can remain denied until the cache TTL expires, even if permissions are later granted, because the denial cache short-circuits the check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Denial cache entry takes precedence over a fresh allow and over an updated permCache (service.go ~line 117) — the denial lookup runs before getCachedIdentityPermissions and only the allow path has outdated-cache fallback, making false denials sticky and uncorrectable by existing invalidation
matched_golden_ids: The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same core problem: a cached `false` (deny) entry causes `checkPermission` to treat the scope as not allowed, contradicting the expectation/comment that cached permissions should "allow access". The candidate generalizes this as deny-cache precedence making false denials sticky, which explains why the `dashboards:uid:dash1=false` entry would still block access.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Denial cache key collides when Name/ParentFolder are empty (rbac/cache.go ~line 30, service.go ~line 117) — key concatenation without boundary separator means "dash1_"+"fold" equals "dash"+"_1fold", and empty-field keys can deny unrelated resource-less checks for the same user/action

P2: List swallows non-cache-miss errors from getCachedIdentityPermissions (service.go ~line 180) — any error is treated as cache miss and retried via getIdentityPermissions, masking transient identity-lookup errors and hiding root causes from logs/metrics

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.List`, `getCachedIdentityPermissions(...)` errors are not distinguished: any non-nil `err` goes to the fallback path and is treated as a cache miss (`permissionCacheUsage` labeled "false"), without logging or counting an error. Since `getCachedIdentityPermissions` can return non-cache-miss errors (e.g., `GetUserIdentifiers` failure or `unsupported identity type`), those can be masked if the subsequent `getIdentityPermissions(...)` call succeeds, losing signal about transient/real issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: In-process client silently loses its cache (rbac.go ~line 101) — ProvideAuthZClient switches newRBACClient's LocalCache (30s expiry) to NoopCache, so every check now pays full server-side processing

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows ProvideAuthZClient no longer constructs the in-process RBAC client with the LocalCache config used by the old newRBACClient path; it now explicitly uses authzlib.WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{}), which makes client-side caching a no-op. That’s a real, diff-grounded performance/behavior change (in-process requests won’t benefit from authzlib client caching anymore), but it’s not a correctness defect by itself—server-side caching logic exists/was expanded in service.go (permCache/permDenialCache), so calls may still avoid DB work even if the client cache is disabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: permDenialCache.Set return error is ignored (service.go ~line 153) — the cache set error is discarded without logging, unlike surrounding code, so a persistently failing cache silently degrades with no observability

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `permDenialCache` is a `*cacheWrap[bool]`, and its `Set` method is invoked as `s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true)` with no assignment/handling, consistent with other cacheWrap usages in tests (e.g., `s.idCache.Set(...)`, `s.permCache.Set(...)`) that also do not capture an error. The `cacheWrap` API shown by usage (`Get` returning `(val, ok)`) suggests `Set` likely does not return an error, so the claim that a `Set` return error is ignored is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New permDenialCache is never included in permission-change invalidation hooks, so stale deny entries can bypass permission grants for up to shortCacheTTL (pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:~153)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `permDenialCache` and makes it a hard short-circuit in `Service.Check`: if the denial key is present, it returns `Allowed: false` without consulting cached permissions or falling back to the DB (`if _, ok := s.permDenialCache.Get(...); ok { ... return Allowed:false }`). The cache is populated on any computed denial (`if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(..., true) }`) and there is no corresponding `Delete`/invalidation path shown in this diff. This means a previously-denied (name,folder,action) check can remain denied for up to `shortCacheTTL` even if permissions are later granted, matching the finding’s stale-deny concern (even if the specific “permission-change invalidation hooks” live elsewhere, this diff itself adds the stale-deny behavior).

adjudication_records.issue_text: userPermDenialCacheKey omits checkReq.IdentityType, causing user and service-account identities with the same UID to share denial cache entries (pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30-32)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, userUID, action, name, parent)` is computed without `checkReq.IdentityType` (see new function in `pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go` and its use in `Service.Check`). This means denial entries are keyed only by `Namespace + UserUID + Action + Name + ParentFolder`. If two different identity types (e.g., user vs service account) can ever share the same `UserUID` string within a namespace, they would share denial cache entries. However, the diff does not show whether such UID collisions are possible, and other caches (e.g., `userPermCacheKey`) also do not include identity type, suggesting this may be an accepted invariant rather than a definite defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Denial-cache lookup short-circuits before cached permissions, letting a cached deny override a fresh cached allow (service.go:116-137)

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, the new permDenialCache lookup happens before any cached-permissions evaluation: it computes permDenialKey and immediately returns Allowed:false if the key exists (service.go, the newly added block before getCachedIdentityPermissions). This means a denial-cache entry will override whatever permCache might say for that same (namespace,user,action,name,parent) check. However, the diff also adds a test explicitly asserting this precedence ("Should deny on explicit cache deny entry"), so it appears intentional; the potential issue is the architectural/correctness risk of stale deny entries causing temporary false-denies even if permCache would allow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cached-permissions fast path never populates the denial cache when allowed == false, making cache-fill order affect behavior (service.go:116-137)

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, a cached-permissions hit only short-circuits when `allowed` is true (service.go:113-137). When cached permissions produce `allowed == false`, the code intentionally falls through to fetch fresh permissions from the DB (`getIdentityPermissions`) and then sets `permDenialCache` if the DB result is also not allowed (`if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(...) }`, service.go:150-154). So the denial cache *is* populated on real denies; it’s just not populated based on the cached-permissions path alone, which would be unsafe with potentially stale caches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getCachedIdentityPermissions returns cache.ErrNotFound for TypeRenderService, silently skipping the cache fast path; also, real errors silently fall through to the full DB path (service.go:~349)

adjudication.rationale: In service.go, Check() and List() treat any non-nil error from getCachedIdentityPermissions() as a cache miss and proceed to the full getIdentityPermissions() path (Check: `if err == nil { ... }` then falls through; List: `if err == nil { ... } else { ... getIdentityPermissions(...) }`). This means real errors (e.g., from `s.GetUserIdentifiers(...)` inside getCachedIdentityPermissions for user/service-account) are not surfaced immediately and can lead to extra work / duplicated DB calls before failing later. Also, getCachedIdentityPermissions explicitly returns `cache.ErrNotFound` for `types.TypeRenderService`, which indeed disables the cache fast path for that identity type, but the diff alone doesn’t show that this is incorrect—more of a design/behavior concern than a clear bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded cache cardinality: permDenialCache keys include specific resource name and parent, so every denied check on a distinct resource creates a new per-user/action/resource cache entry, causing key-space and memory blowup

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `permDenialCache` and a denial key that includes per-request resource identifiers: `userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, userUID, action, name, parent)` (added in `cache.go`). In `Service.Check`, on every denied check it executes `s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true)` and later short-circuits denies if that key exists. Because `name` and `parent` can vary per resource, this creates a distinct cache entry per user/action/resource(/parent) with no size bound shown in the diff, so repeated denies across many unique resources can grow cache key-space and memory usage significantly (potential DoS/resource exhaustion).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Denial cache is not invalidated on permission/role changes: after a user is granted access to a previously denied resource, the stale deny entry short-circuits Check and returns Allowed: false until TTL expiry

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `permDenialCache` and makes it a hard short-circuit in `Service.Check`: if `s.permDenialCache.Get(...); ok` it immediately returns `Allowed: false` without consulting cached permissions or the DB (service.go around the new `permDenialKey` block). Denial entries are written whenever `!allowed` (`s.permDenialCache.Set(...)`). There is no invalidation path shown for when permissions/roles change, so a previously denied check can remain denied until the cache TTL expires, even if the underlying permissions have since been granted. This is a correctness regression compared to the prior behavior where cache misses/outdated data fell back to DB.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Errors from getCachedIdentityPermissions are silently swallowed in Check; real errors (GetUserIdentifiers failure, unsupported identity type) are discarded and redundant work is done before re-encountering them in getIdentityPermissions

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, the call `cachedPerms, err := s.getCachedIdentityPermissions(...)` only takes the cache-fast-path when `err == nil`; any non-nil error is treated like a cache miss (it just falls through after incrementing `permissionCacheUsage` as "false"). This means real errors from `getCachedIdentityPermissions` (e.g., `GetUserIdentifiers` failure in the user/service-account case, or the explicit `fmt.Errorf("unsupported identity type: %s", idType)` in the `default:` branch) are not acted on at that point and will trigger an additional call to `getIdentityPermissions(...)`, likely re-hitting the same error path and doing redundant work. The behavior is more about inefficiency/observability than a definite correctness break visible in the diff, since the later `getIdentityPermissions` error handling will still return an error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Metric mislabeling on cache-hit-then-deny path: permissionCacheUsage 'false'/'true' is emitted after a store fetch even though the cache was used, distorting cache-usage metrics on the deny-via-cached-perms path

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, when `getCachedIdentityPermissions(...)` returns cached perms (`err == nil`) but `checkPermission(...)` returns `allowed == false`, the code falls through and unconditionally increments `permissionCacheUsage` with label `"false"` (`s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("false", checkReq.Action).Inc()`). This records a cache miss even though the permission cache was successfully read and evaluated. The metric only records `"true"` on the early-return allow path, so the cache-hit-but-deny path is miscounted as `"false"`, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Denial cache is never invalidated on permission changes, causing stale deny results after access is granted; it must participate in the same invalidation flow as permCache

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `permDenialCache` and makes it a hard short-circuit in `Service.Check`: if `permDenialCache.Get(...)` hits, it immediately returns `Allowed: false` without consulting the permission store (`service.go` around the new `permDenialKey` block). The cache is populated on any computed denial (`if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(..., true) }`) and there is no corresponding invalidation/delete shown anywhere in the diff (only TTL via `newCacheWrap(..., shortCacheTTL)`). This means a user who was denied and then later granted access can continue to be denied until the denial entry expires, which is stale incorrect behavior introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Denial cache key uses raw UserUID without distinguishing identity type, so anonymous checks (empty UserUID) collapse onto shared keys causing cross-identity denial sharing

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, the denial cache key is built as userPermDenialCacheKey(ns, checkReq.UserUID, action, name, parentFolder) and checked before any branching on IdentityType. The key does not include identity type, and getCachedIdentityPermissions explicitly supports identity types that may not have a meaningful/unique userID (e.g., TypeAnonymous, TypeRenderService). If those identities use an empty or non-unique UserUID, denial entries would collide and be shared across identities for the same (namespace, action, name, parentFolder), causing incorrect denials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Denial cache key fields joined with '_' without escaping can collide (e.g., name='a_b', parent='c' vs name='a', parent='b_c'), producing incorrect deny results

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, userUID, action, name, parent)` in `pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go` which builds the cache key by concatenating fields with '_' (e.g., `... + "_" + name + "_" + parent`). In `Service.Check` this key is used to short-circuit and return `Allowed: false` if present. Because the fields are not escaped or length-delimited, different (name,parent) combinations containing '_' can produce the same string key (e.g., name="a_b", parent="c" vs name="a", parent="b_c"), which can cause incorrect deny decisions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions no longer consult the cache after cache lookup moved to getCachedIdentityPermissions; other internal callers silently lose caching, changing the prior self-caching contract with no compile-time signal

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the cache read paths in `getUserPermissions` (deleted `permCache.Get` block) and `getAnonymousPermissions` (deleted `permCache.Get` block), while introducing a separate `getCachedIdentityPermissions` used by `Check` and `List`. This means any other internal code paths that still call `getUserPermissions`/`getAnonymousPermissions` (or `getIdentityPermissions` without first calling `getCachedIdentityPermissions`) would no longer benefit from cache hits, changing the prior self-caching behavior with no compiler signal. The existence of such other callers isn’t verifiable from the shown diff, so the impact is an architectural/perf concern rather than a proven correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale denial entries deny access even after a permission grant because the denial cache is checked first and uses a different cache key that is not refreshed by permission-cache invalidation, extending the stale-denial window

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, the new permDenialCache is consulted first and returns an immediate deny if the denial key is present (service.go:113-121). That denial entry is only ever set on a negative decision (service.go:150-153) and there is no code in the diff that clears/refreshes permDenialCache when permissions later become allowed. As a result, once a denial is cached for (namespace,userUID,action,name,parent), subsequent calls will be denied until the denial cache TTL expires, even if the underlying permissions (DB or permCache) would now allow. The part of the finding about “permission-cache invalidation” specifically isn’t shown in this diff, but the stale-denial behavior due to deny-first logic is verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cache-hit denial path defeats the purpose of the cache: when permCache is hit but denied, code falls through to a full DB fetch before populating the denial cache, so denials are uncached on first hit and add DB load
matched_golden_ids: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that when the permission cache contains a denial, the code ignores that cached result and proceeds to a DB lookup, i.e., cached denials aren’t trusted. This is the same core asymmetric cache-trust behavior described in the golden comment (cached grants are used immediately while cached denials trigger a fresh fetch), though the candidate emphasizes performance/DB load rather than the security risk from stale cached grants.

adjudication_records.issue_text: List treats non-NotFound errors from getCachedIdentityPermissions as cache misses, masking the root error, duplicating user-identifier lookups, and paying two failing DB paths on persistent failure

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.List`, the new logic treats any non-nil error from `getCachedIdentityPermissions` as a cache miss (`if err == nil { ... } else { ... permissions, err = s.getIdentityPermissions(...) }`). But `getCachedIdentityPermissions` can return real errors (e.g., from `s.GetUserIdentifiers` for user/service-account types, or `fmt.Errorf("unsupported identity type")`). Those errors are ignored rather than propagated/logged, and the code then re-enters `getIdentityPermissions`, which will typically redo the same identifier lookup/DB work and likely fail again on persistent failure. This is a real, diff-introduced inefficiency and error-masking concern, but not necessarily a functional correctness defect since the second path will still return an error if the underlying failure persists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: permDenialCache.Set error is silently ignored, so with a distributed cache backend the denial cache may silently never warm

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, when a permission check is denied the code calls `s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true)` and does not inspect or propagate any returned error (if any). This makes failure to populate the denial cache non-obvious at the call site and could reduce cache effectiveness (extra DB lookups) if the underlying cache write fails. The diff does not show whether `cacheWrap.Set` can actually error or whether it logs internally, nor does it show a distributed cache backend, so the impact described is not fully verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Denial cache key concatenates userUID, action, name, and parent with unescaped '_' separators, allowing key collisions that can deny access to the wrong resource

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, userUID, action, name, parent)` which builds a cache key by concatenating fields with literal "_" separators: `namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent` (pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go). In `Service.Check`, this key is used for an early-deny lookup (`if _, ok := s.permDenialCache.Get(...); ok { return Allowed:false }`) and is populated on any denied check. Because the components are not escaped or length-delimited, different (userUID, action, name, parent) tuples can produce the same string when any component contains "_" (e.g., userUID="a_b", action="c" vs userUID="a", action="b_c"), which could incorrectly deny access to a different resource.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In-process client switched to NoopCache so service-level caches are the only caching; code relying on client-level cache to absorb bursts now hits the store directly — verify this deliberate change

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show the in-process client cache being disabled: `ProvideAuthZClient` replaces `newRBACClient(channel, tracer)` with `authzlib.NewClient(..., authzlib.WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{}), ...)`, and `NoopCache.Get` always returns `cache.ErrNotFound`. Remote clients still use a real local cache in `newRemoteRBACClient` (via `cache.NewLocalCache`). This is a deliberate behavior change that can affect performance/burst absorption characteristics at the client layer, even though the service now has/uses service-level caches (`getCachedIdentityPermissions`, `permDenialCache`). Whether this is acceptable is an architectural/intent question rather than a provable correctness bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: permDenialCache in pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116-160 has no invalidation path when user permissions change, causing stale denials (potential access bug) after permission grants until shortCacheTTL expires

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `permDenialCache` and makes it authoritative in `Service.Check`: if the denial key is present it immediately returns `Allowed: false` before consulting cached perms or the DB (`Check` adds an early return on `permDenialCache.Get(...)`). The cache is populated on any computed denial (`if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(...) }`). There is no diff-shown invalidation mechanism tied to permission/role changes; only expiration via `shortCacheTTL` is implied by `newCacheWrap[bool](..., shortCacheTTL)`. This can indeed cause temporary stale denials after a permission grant until TTL expires, but whether that is an actual defect vs an acceptable tradeoff isn’t provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Test at service_test.go:943-963 ('Fallback to the database on outdated cache') tests an ordinary cache miss, not the actual stale-denial scenario (denial cache entry for a resource that has since been granted), masking the missing invalidation coverage

adjudication.rationale: The added test `Fallback to the database on outdated cache` sets `permCache` to a map missing `dash2`, so `checkPermission` will return not-allowed and the code falls back to `getIdentityPermissions` (DB) and succeeds. That exercises a stale/partial positive-permissions cache, not the new `permDenialCache` behavior. The new early-return denial path (`if _, ok := s.permDenialCache.Get(...); ok { return Allowed:false }`) has no test for the “stale denial after grant” scenario (deny entry present but should be overridden by DB due to permission changes), i.e., there’s no invalidation/override coverage for `permDenialCache`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: The cached-deny fallthrough path in Check (service.go:116-141) — cache hit with allowed=false falling through to a full getIdentityPermissions fetch before caching the denial — is untested

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, a cache hit can still produce `allowed == false` (via `getCachedIdentityPermissions` + `checkPermission`) and then intentionally falls through to `getIdentityPermissions`, only caching the denial afterward (`if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(...) }`). The newly added tests cover: cached allow (`Allow based on cached permissions`), cache miss/outdated leading to DB allow (`Fallback...`), and an existing `permDenialCache` short-circuit (`Should deny on explicit cache deny entry`). None of the tests exercise the specific path where cached permissions are present but deny (e.g., missing/false entry for the checked resource), DB is consulted, DB also denies, and then `permDenialCache` is populated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: New getCachedIdentityPermissions edge branches (TypeAnonymous, TypeRenderService, default error) in service.go:342-368 are untested; the default branch changes observable behavior since errors are silently swallowed in Check/List, causing a second doomed fetch

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `getCachedIdentityPermissions` with new switch branches for `TypeAnonymous`, `TypeRenderService`, and a `default` that returns `fmt.Errorf("unsupported identity type")` (service.go ~303-337). The newly added tests (`TestService_CacheCheck`, `TestService_CacheList`) only exercise the user/service-account path (via `Subject: "user:..."`) and do not cover the anonymous/render-service/default branches, so the “untested branches” part is grounded. Also, both `Check` and `List` treat any error from `getCachedIdentityPermissions` as a cache miss and fall back to `getIdentityPermissions` (i.e., they only special-case `err == nil`), so a non-ErrNotFound error like the `default` case will be ignored and followed by a second attempt that will likely fail again—an inefficiency/behavioral change in logging/metrics rather than a clear correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: New exported NoopCache in pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:238-251 has zero test coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new exported `type NoopCache struct{}` with `Get/Set/Delete` methods in `pkg/services/authz/rbac.go` (used in `ProvideAuthZClient` via `authzlib.WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{})`). The added/updated tests cover cached permission behavior in `Service` but do not reference or exercise `NoopCache`, so the claim of zero direct test coverage for this new type is supported by the diff. This is a test/coverage concern rather than a verifiable functional defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: TestService_CacheList (service_test.go:1291-1324) covers only the cache-hit branch; the cache-miss List fallback path (cache.ErrNotFound → store consultation) is untested

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the newly added TestService_CacheList pre-populates s.permCache (and idCache) and therefore only exercises the List() cache-hit branch (`permissions, err := s.getCachedIdentityPermissions...; if err == nil { ... }`). The new cache-miss fallback branch (`else { ... permissions, err = s.getIdentityPermissions(...) }`) is not covered by this new cache-specific test, so a reviewer could reasonably ask for an explicit test of the cache.ErrNotFound → store fallback behavior for List. The diff excerpt doesn’t show whether existing TestService_List cases already cover that fallback path, so the “untested” claim beyond this new test can’t be fully verified from the provided context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated identity-type/cache-key resolution logic between getCachedIdentityPermissions and getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions risks divergence; extract a shared resolvePermissionCacheKey helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces getCachedIdentityPermissions with identity-type branching and cache-key construction (anonymousPermCacheKey, GetUserIdentifiers + userPermCacheKey), but getUserPermissions and getAnonymousPermissions still independently compute the same keys (userPermKey := userPermCacheKey(...), anonPermKey := anonymousPermCacheKey(...)) for singleflight and caching. This is real duplication created/left by the change and could diverge if key formats or identity handling evolves, though it is not a functional defect visible in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent error swallowing in Check and List: errors from getCachedIdentityPermissions are indistinguishable from cache miss and silently fall through to DB path with no logging; distinguish cache.ErrNotFound from real errors and log/track unexpected ones

adjudication.rationale: In both `Service.Check` and `Service.List`, the code treats any non-nil error from `getCachedIdentityPermissions(...)` the same as a cache miss: it simply falls back to `getIdentityPermissions(...)` without distinguishing `cache.ErrNotFound` from other errors. For example, in `Check` it does `cachedPerms, err := ...; if err == nil { ... }` and otherwise proceeds, and in `List` it only logs if the subsequent DB call fails. Since `getCachedIdentityPermissions` can return real errors (e.g., from `s.GetUserIdentifiers(...)` or unsupported identity type), those can be silently ignored if the DB path succeeds, reducing observability and potentially masking cache/ID lookup issues (and causing unnecessary extra work). This is a diff-grounded error-handling/metrics concern rather than a clear functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Double identifier/DB lookup on cache miss in Check: getCachedIdentityPermissions resolves GetUserIdentifiers before discovering perm cache is empty, then fallback getIdentityPermissions resolves identifiers again

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, the new fast-path calls getCachedIdentityPermissions(ctx, ns, idType, userUID, action). For TypeUser/TypeServiceAccount, getCachedIdentityPermissions calls s.GetUserIdentifiers(...) before checking s.permCache (userPermCacheKey uses userIdentifiers.UID). If the permission entry is missing/outdated, Check then falls back to s.getIdentityPermissions(...), which (via getUserPermissions) also calls s.GetUserIdentifiers(...) again. This is a verifiable duplicated identifier lookup on cache-miss/fallback; it’s a performance/efficiency concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: NoopCache defined locally in pkg/services/authz/rbac.go instead of being contributed to the cache package/authzlib; NewClient's caller-supplied cache API forces a noop stub, and the caching asymmetry between in-process and remote clients is implicit with no comment

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a locally-defined `NoopCache` in `pkg/services/authz/rbac.go` and uses it in `ProvideAuthZClient` when constructing the in-process client (`authzlib.NewClient(..., authzlib.WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{}), ...)`). Meanwhile `newRemoteRBACClient` constructs the remote client with a real `cache.NewLocalCache(...)`. This creates an implicit caching asymmetry between in-process vs remote clients, and the noop cache implementation is embedded in this service package rather than shared via `cache`/`authzlib` (no comment in the diff explaining why). This is a concrete maintainability/architecture concern grounded in the shown changes, but not a demonstrable functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cache orchestration concerns inlined into Check handler while List uses a different, inconsistent caching pattern (no denial cache); caching policy should live in the permission-resolution layer, not each handler

adjudication.rationale: The diff does inline cache-orchestration logic into the `Check` handler: it introduces an explicit denial cache key (`permDenialKey := userPermDenialCacheKey(...)`) and an early-return deny path in `Service.Check` before permission resolution (`if _, ok := s.permDenialCache.Get(...); ok { ... return Allowed: false }`). It also performs a cached-permissions fast path in the handler (`getCachedIdentityPermissions` + `checkPermission`) and only falls back to `getIdentityPermissions` on miss or non-allow. By contrast, `Service.List` uses a different pattern: it calls `getCachedIdentityPermissions` and on miss directly falls back to `getIdentityPermissions`, with no analogous denial-cache behavior. This is an inconsistency introduced by the change and supports the architectural concern that caching policy is now split between handlers and resolution logic, rather than fully encapsulated in the permission-resolution layer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: permissionCacheUsage metric semantics become confusing/misleading after refactor: 'false' no longer uniformly means served-from-store, increments occur at a different layer, and label pairs mean different things per branch, changing dashboard/alert meaning without version bump

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes where/when `permissionCacheUsage` is incremented and what the "true/false" label effectively represents. Previously it was tied to `permCache.Get` in `getUserPermissions` (hit => "true", miss => "false"). Now it’s emitted in higher-level handlers: in `Service.Check`, it increments "true" both for `permDenialCache` hits and for allowed decisions from cached perms, but it increments "false" unconditionally before the DB fetch even in the case where `getCachedIdentityPermissions` succeeded but `checkPermission` returned `allowed == false` (i.e., cache was consulted but didn’t satisfy the check). In `Service.List`, "true" means cached permissions returned without error, while "false" means cache miss/error and then DB fallback. This makes the metric semantics inconsistent across branches/layers and potentially misleading ("false" is no longer uniformly "served from store").

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deleted test coverage for cache-hit behavior in getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions: removed 'should return permissions from cache if available' case leaves internal cache-read behavior untested, especially anonymous permission caching which has no equivalent new test

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the explicit cache-read branches inside `getUserPermissions` and `getAnonymousPermissions` (the `permCache.Get(...)` checks were deleted), and the old unit test case “should return permissions from cache if available” in `TestService_getUserPermissions` was also removed. Cache-hit behavior is now implemented in the new `getCachedIdentityPermissions` and exercised for user identities via `TestService_CacheCheck` / `TestService_CacheList`, but there is no new test covering the anonymous cache-hit path (`types.TypeAnonymous` branch using `anonymousPermCacheKey` in `getCachedIdentityPermissions`). This is a specific, diff-grounded test coverage gap for the new caching structure, not a demonstrated functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Denial cache is never invalidated and overrides fresh allow decisions — cached denial wins even when permission cache says allow, and with no invalidation path permission grants are blocked for up to shortCacheTTL; denial key also lacks permission-version so stale-permission denials can poison granted permissions (pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:117,153)

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, the new permDenialCache is consulted first and immediately returns Allowed:false on a cache hit (service.go:113-121) before evaluating cached permission maps or querying the store. The denial entry is written whenever a DB-backed check returns not allowed (service.go:150-153). The diff shows no invalidation/update path for these denial entries, and the denial key (namespace/userUID/action/name/parent) has no versioning component (cache.go) to distinguish permission-state changes. As a result, a previously cached denial can override a later (fresh) allow decision for up to shortCacheTTL, producing incorrect authorization outcomes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Denial cache key collision via unescaped _/: delimiters — userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates action, name, parent with _ and no escaping, so distinct tuples collide and a denial for one resource silently denies another (pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30-32)
matched_golden_ids: The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying problem: `userPermDenialCacheKey` builds cache keys by concatenating multiple components with `_` (and other delimiters) without escaping or structure, which can create ambiguous keys and collisions when components contain underscores or are empty, leading to incorrect denial cache hits affecting permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Denial cached for checks with empty Name blankets all unnamed checks — a transiently incomplete permission fetch can poison cache for all subsequent unnamed user/action/folder checks until TTL expiry (pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:117,153)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a denial cache in `Service.Check`: it computes `permDenialKey := userPermDenialCacheKey(..., checkReq.Name, checkReq.ParentFolder)` and immediately returns `Allowed: false` on a cache hit, and it writes to this cache whenever `!allowed` (service.go). If `checkReq.Name` is empty, the key collapses to the same value for all checks sharing (namespace,userUID,action,parentFolder,""), so a single cached denial will apply to all subsequent unnamed checks for that tuple until TTL. The diff does not show whether empty `Name` is a valid/meaningful case for `Check` or whether such broad denial is incorrect, so this is a concrete edge-case concern but not a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Denial-cache hit path skips identity re-validation — denial keyed on raw checkReq.UserUID is returned before GetUserIdentifiers resolution, so UID reuse after user deletion inherits the old denial (pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:117-121)

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check(), the new early-return denial-cache path looks up permDenialCache using userPermDenialCacheKey(..., checkReq.UserUID, ...) before any call to GetUserIdentifiers (service.go:113-121). In contrast, permission caching for users/service accounts is keyed on the resolved canonical UID from GetUserIdentifiers (getCachedIdentityPermissions uses userIdentifiers.UID). This inconsistency means a denial can be applied based on the raw incoming identifier without identity resolution/normalization, so if the raw identifier can map to a different underlying user over time (e.g., reuse/aliasing), an old denial entry could incorrectly deny a different identity.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Coverage silently removed for the old cache-hit path — the test asserting getUserPermissions returns cached permissions was deleted without an equivalent assertion that the singleflight path still consults permCache (pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:342-349)

adjudication.rationale: The deleted test covered a cache-hit branch that no longer exists in `getUserPermissions`: the diff removes the `permCache.Get(...)` check from `getUserPermissions` and instead introduces `getCachedIdentityPermissions`, which is called from `Service.Check` and `Service.List` before falling back to `getIdentityPermissions`. Equivalent cache-hit coverage is added via `TestService_CacheCheck` ("Allow based on cached permissions") and `TestService_CacheList` ("List based on cached permissions"), which explicitly preload `s.permCache` and assert behavior. The finding’s claim that coverage was removed “without an equivalent assertion” (and that the singleflight path should still consult `permCache`) misreads the refactor: cache consultation moved out of the singleflight-backed functions.
